ledger.x: c. 450 BC: 'Around the middle of the 5th century BC, they moved south into Oenotria, pushing the indigenous Oenotrians, Chones, and Lauternoi into the mountainous interior'; 'in what is now southern Italy', the modern Basilicata's inhabitants 'are still called Lucani'. The Greek coastal cities (Thurii, Heraclea…

c. 390 BC: after their victory over the Thurii near Laus in 390 BC the Lucanians 'established their dominion over the interior' of Bruttium and many Greek outposts; the page says 'this probably took place after' 390, so the year is a bound, not a date.

c. 356 BC: the Bruttii break away: 'The rise of the Bruttii is dated by ancient authors to approximately 356 BC'; they 'became numerous and powerful enough to defy the Lucanians' (mirror of the bruttii found event).
282 BC: 'the Lucanians and Bruttians besieged Thurii in 282 BC, and a Roman army under Gaius Fabricius Luscinus defeated them'.

281-272 BC: the Pyrrhic War; Pyrrhus 'landed in 281 BC' and the Lucanians 'were among the first to declare for him'; Heraclea 'in Lucania' (280); 'about ten triumphs recorded between 282 and 272 BC' over the southern peoples.
272 BC: Tarentum falls; the war ends.

272 BC: the Lucanians are 'reduced to subjection in a ten-year campaign (272)'; they stay on their land as allies of Rome, tinted from roman-republic (vassal_start lucanians 272); they 'espoused the cause of Hannibal' in 216 and the land was 'ravaged by both armies'.
91 BC: the Lucanians rise in the Social War: they 'took part with the Samnites against Rome' (Lucanians page; the Lucania page has 90-88 BC; roman-republic /ledger/129 has 91).

91 BC: the Lucanian land passes to the Italian confederation of the Social War (Cliopatria's Italian City-States, -91..-88); the war 'gave the finishing stroke' to the region's decline and Lucania 'fell into decay'.

wars.name: Pyrrhic War (Lucanian theatre)
wars.outcome: Roman victory; the Lucanians 'reduced to subjection' (272)

certainty.note: Lucania has no surveyed border; the Basilicata region stands for it.
